newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Capital market needs reform, says SEC chief.
newsitem.headline: Capital market needs reform, says SEC chief.

text.p: The Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Haroonur Rashid, said on Wednesday Bangladesh's main Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) needed automation to ensure transparency in the capital market.
"We are also giving emphasis to setting up a central depository system (CDS), the scripless trading that will foster the market," he told a meeting of the Economic Reporters Forum.
The chief of the market watchdog said the SEC was negotiating with donors to mobilise funds for the financing the projects.
Imtiyaz Husain, chairman of the DSE, said the 25-year- old market regulatory acts required reforms to prevent another market crash like that which happened recently.

The stock market got off to a flying start as soon as the new government took power in June last year. The DSE index rose to more than 3,600 from less than 1,000. But it fell again below 1,800 after the government introduced stricter circuit breakers or caps on price fluctuaion in November.

Salman F. Rahman, former president of Bangladesh Federation of Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said the capital market lacked instituional investors. "This is a fundamental problem of the capital market," he said.
